summary: Steel Forest Service lookout in Wayne County, MO, about 120 ft, described by the Coast and Geodetic Survey in 1963; no later source describes its condition.

facts.design: Four-legged steel structure with an enclosed observing room at the top
facts.status_note: Last described in a 1963 survey record; no source found describes its condition since.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mark Twain National Forest)

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey first observed and described the tower. The survey record gives no construction date.

evidence.supports: Described by the Coast and Geodetic Survey in 1963
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1963 (VBM)

evidence.supports: Four-legged steel structure with an enclosed observing room at the top
evidence.quote: 4 LEG STEEL STRUCTURE WITH AN ENCLOSED OBSERVING ROOM AT
THE OVERALL HEIGHT OF THE STRUCTURE IS ABOUT 120 FEET

evidence.supports: Owned and operated by the U.S. Forest Service
evidence.quote: IT IS OWNED AND OPERATED BY THE U.S. FOREST SERVICE.

evidence.supports: Directions begin at the junction of County Roads A and O
evidence.quote: TO REACH THE STATION FROM THE JUNCTION OF COUNTY ROADS A

evidence.supports: East on Road O for 2.05 miles
evidence.quote: AND O IN WILLIAMSVILLE, GO EAST ON ROAD O FOR 2.05 MILES

evidence.supports: North on a gravel road for 1.1 miles to the tower
evidence.quote: GRAVELED ROAD FOR 1.1 MILES TO THE LOOKOUT TOWER

evidence.supports: History section has one entry, a 1963 first observation
Mark Twain National Forest named for the site

notes_for_editor: Height converted from 'about 120 feet' (36.6 m). Brief had no height. No source found on construction, staffing, fires, access or current condition; the only site-specific record is the 1963 survey description. nhlr.org Missouri page for this tower returned 404, and the cached Missouri NHLR listing has no Williamsville entry. firetower.org Missouri former-site register lists only Grassy and Gypsy, so this tower is not on it. Unread leads: MoDOT historic highway maps (could date the tower) and a Missouri Life article (403 when fetched). A Mindat 'Williamsville Tower prospect' is a mine record, not used.
